confidence_notes: I based the food, coffee and beer prices on web searches of crowdsourced cost-of-living data. The main source was Numbeo's Bariloche page (July 2026 update): cappuccino about $3.84–3.92, domestic draft pint about $5.00–5.21, cheap meal about $16.77 and mid-range meal for two about $57.08. Expatistan's May 2026 peso prices broadly agree. Both sources rest on few data points, and Argentina's inflation and exchange-rate swings make prices change quickly. I set inexp_meal_1p a little below Numbeo's average to fit a typical inexpensive restaurant. I didn't search for cocktail or wine prices. I estimated them from local price relationships to beer and Argentina's cheap domestic wine, so they are less certain. Accommodation prices are my own overall estimates, not taken from any search or listing. July is ski high season in Bariloche (Cerro Catedral), which pushes room rates up, so these are the least certain anchors. The RBA rate came from a web search result, not from reading the RBA page directly.
comparable_city_reasoning: I used Numbeo and Expatistan figures for Bariloche itself. For cocktails, wine and accommodation, I compared against Mendoza and Buenos Aires, adding a premium for a ski resort in high season.
